moves.why: Same plan as game one, but now I know: small-first is mandatory. Bore 0 it is.
same plan: 2-pt floor beats 1-pt seal; bores 2 and 5 are symmetric so far, picking 2 to claim the upper half while leaving 5 for later
same as last game — claim a floor while they exist; smalls are the whole game
Same opening as game one — claim a floor before anyone seals shelves. Bore 3 keeps me near the action.

Last game I wasted a large here. This time I take the 5th floor myself — 2 points, and I become the only player with 2 floors. Seat 1 is the big threat; denying them the 5th floor matters more than banking.

only open-floor bore left and four players still alive; the 2 points are unrecoverable later. I'll have plenty of large pucks to seal in subsequent rounds. This is the obvious repeatable play — same as turn 1 last game
all floors gone, all shelves equal — any large scores 1, no smalls to play
sealing bore 1 denies seat 1 (who owns floor at bore 2) AND seat 2 (floor at bore 1) — two rival floors buried with one large

I claim shelf of bore 5 (my floor) — it pairs my two best claims and the shelf is uncontested. Bore 4 is more important strategically because it's seat 1's floor, but sealing my own shelf first doesn't let opponent steal it. Wait — sealing anywhere gives ME 1 point. I want to seal one whose floor is MINE so I get 2+1=3. Bore 5's floor is mine. Take it.

bore 4 has my small in it; sealing it gives me 5 pts (floor+shelf). Sealing bores 2 or 3 also gives 3+0=3 each and lets other players score on the next round. Sealing my own bore is the +1 over the alternatives; I keep pace with seat 0
two equal shelves left, identical outcome either way
bore 3 is the only open shelf; taking it gets me a 4th point and the game ends
